range: a009c65..10abb07 on specs/requests/02-client-participants.md — a .fix.json for this spec exists, so the sweeps ran over the added and modified lines and the rules they touch, and every rule that changed was checked against the whole document for contradiction
request: Client participants: let a client contact hold a principal in an organization and take part in requests raised for their client, without becoming a member of the organization.

findings.claim: the case's steps cannot reach the state its expected result needs — minting two invitations for one address invalidates the first token, so no ordering of the two acceptances produces 'a ClientMembership, then 409 accountIsClient'

witness.detail: TC-02-INT-16 (:979): 'Mint two client invitations for the same address and client, keeping both tokens - the state two simultaneous invites can leave (edge case 21). Accept one token, then the other.' Expected (:981): 'the first acceptance creates exactly one ClientMembership; the second answers 409 accountIsClient and creates nothing.' Requirement 19 (:222): 'at most one live pending invitation per (email, organization), whichever kind it is.' TC-02-INT-15 (:971) spells out what that does to the earlier token: 'the staff invitation's status is invalidated and the client one is pending; accepting the staff token answers 400 INVITE_MESSAGES.tokenInvalid and writes no membership of either kind.' So after the second mint the first token is invalidated, and neither ordering works: accepting the invalidated token first answers 400 tokenInvalid and creates no ClientMembership, and accepting the surviving token first leaves the invalidated one to answer 400 tokenInvalid rather than 409 accountIsClient. Edge case 21 (:580) says the two-live-pending state arises only because 'nothing serializes the two writes' — a race the steps neither describe nor stage. The code is the same: apps/api/src/invitations/invitations.service.ts:106-111 runs invitation.updateMany({ where: { email, organizationId, status: 'pending' }, data: { status: 'invalidated' } }) in the same transaction as every create, for any role.

findings.suggestedFix: say in the steps how two live pending rows are reached — the only mechanism this spec describes is edge case 21's unserialized race, so either the case seeds the second pending row directly and says so, or it becomes the sequence it can actually run (mint, re-mint, accept the surviving token, then accept the superseded one for 400 tokenInvalid) and the acceptance guarantee edge case 21 rests on is observed instead by accepting a second live token for an address that already holds an active ClientMembership

findings.claim: the clause added to requirement 23 — that a request left with a removed client user may be reassigned to another active client user of the project's client — is observed by no case; every reassignment in the cases targets a member

witness.detail: Requirement 23 (:240): 'An admin or manager may then reassign it - to a member, or to another active client user of the project's client - and the reassignment writes a RequestEvent with action = assignee_changed carrying both display names in oldLabel / newLabel.' TC-02-INT-12 (:947), the only reassignment case, asserts only 'reassigning it to a member succeeds and writes assignee_changed with both display-name snapshots'. TC-02-INT-10 exercises assigneeKind 'client' on POST .../requests alone, and TC-02-INT-18 only asserts that a client principal cannot call reassign. Nothing observes assigneeKind: 'client' on POST .../requests/{id}/reassign, although the API Contracts section (:549-554) states that route accepts it and adds projectRequiredForClient, contactProjectMismatch and clientUserUnavailable to it.

findings.suggestedFix: extend TC-02-INT-12 with a second reassignment, to another active client user of the same client, asserting 200, assigneeKind 'client' on the row, and the assignee_changed event carrying both labels

findings.claim: the enumeration of nav ids that must be absent for a client principal is still short by one of the rows the sidebar draws

witness.detail: grep -n "testId: '" apps/web/src/layout/Sidebar.tsx returns ten navigation entries: nav-time-tracking (:64), nav-members (:75), sidebar-requests-link (:84), nav-projects (:97), nav-clients (:108), nav-envelopes (:122), nav-documents (:131), nav-outbox (:140), nav-settings (:159) and settings-tab-holidays (:171) — the last is the Holidays row, pushed into the same Settings group as nav-settings and gated on ViewHolidays. The spec's row (:641) names nav-members, nav-projects, nav-clients, nav-time-tracking, nav-envelopes, nav-documents, nav-outbox and nav-settings and stops. Requirement 12 ('exactly one row') still governs, so nothing wrong is drawn; the enumeration is simply incomplete.

findings.suggestedFix: add settings-tab-holidays to the absent list

findings.claim: the refusal a caller without the capability receives from POST /api/invitations changes for role = 'client', from the message that route answers today to this spec's own

witness.detail: The contract (:509): '403 CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES.manageForbidden when role = client and the caller lacks the capability, staff or client principal.' apps/api/src/invitations/invitations.service.ts:66-73 refuses every caller who is not an active admin or manager of the session's organization with 403 { message: INVITE_MESSAGES.permissionDenied } ('You do not have permission to invite members'), and does so before the body is validated at all — so the same caller sending role='client' is answered a different message after this spec than before it. manage-client-users and the invite permission are held by exactly the same two roles, so nothing about who may invite changes; only what the refused caller is told.

findings.suggestedFix: none — the spec states its rule in full; this is recorded so a person can confirm the changed message on an existing route was meant
